children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were higher late Thursday morning, as the Canadian oilseed continues its see-saw week of rangebound trading. Today's gains have moderated from double-digit increases earlier.
"It's turnaround Thursday," an analyst said, adding he can't make "hide nor hair at what's driving things up." "We could be down tomorrow again," the analyst said.

Crude oil was on the rise after five vessels struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Support from crude spilled over into European rapeseed and the Chicago soy complex, although soymeal was still lower. Malaysian palm oil was weaker on the day.
The January canola contract was above its 20- and 200-day moving averages but remained below its 50- and 100-day averages.
Canola crush margins stepped back, with the January position retreating by nearly C$15 at C$225.34 per tonne above the futures.
The Canadian dollar nudged up late Thursday morning with the loonie at 69.87 U.S. cents, compared to Wednesday's close of 69.80.
Approximately 34,450 canola contracts were traded as of 11:09 a.m. EST with prices in Canadian dollars per metric tonne:

Price      Change 
Jan       777.90     up 6.70 
Mar       787.80     up 6.40 
May       794.90     up 6.30 
Jul       795.80     up 6.70
